pr_comments: As a whole looks pretty good, though with the growing number of null-related parameters, I think we will at some point need to condense into one "super parameter" (e.g. `dict` of some sorts).

@jreback I think I will first try to get this feature-complete by adding in support for nullable float and string dtypes. Then I can spit out the inferencing changes. Marking this as draft in the meantime.
Currently progress blocked on StringArray support by #40839

Hello @lithomas1! Thanks for updating this PR. We checked the lines you've touched for [PEP 8](https://www.python.org/dev/peps/pep-0008) issues, and found:

















There are currently no PEP 8 issues detected in this Pull Request. Cheers! :beers: 

##### Comment last updated at 2021-06-05 02:36:55 UTC

@lithomas1 I think that the resulting dtype when using `use_nullable_dtypes=True` should not depend on whether NAs are present or not (IIUC the current state of the PR will eg only use nullable Int64 dtype if there is at least one missing value in the column, and otherwise return plain int64 dtype?) 
Having it depend on the presence if missing values introduces "value-dependent" behaviour, which we generally try to avoid. The nullable vs non-nullable dtype *can* behave somewhat differently, and so IMO it's better to return consistent dtypes. For example, assume you have a bunch of CSV files with the same structure (columns and types), then ideally you get the same inferred dtypes for each file (except for the corner case of all-missing data, of course).
the downside of that is it locks the user in to non-consolidated columns, with associated perf penalties.
Depends on #41412, but we need to discuss the correct behavior in #42973.
@lithomas1 this might be easier these days?
Thanks for the pull request, but it appears to have gone stale. Feel free to reopen when you have the time to revisit. Closing to clear out the queue.

issue_context.title: ENH: add option to get nullable dtypes to pd.read_csv
issue_context.body:
- [x] I have checked that this issue has not already been reported.

- [x] I have confirmed this bug exists on the latest version of pandas.

- [ ] (optional) I have confirmed this bug exists on the master branch of pandas.

---

#### Code Sample, a copy-pastable example

```python
In[2]: import pandas as pd
In[3]: s = pd.Series([1, 2, None, 3], dtype=pd.UInt64Dtype())
In[4]: s
Out[4]: 
0       1
1       2
2    <NA>
3       3
dtype: UInt64
In[5]: df = pd.DataFrame({"a":s})
In[6]: df
Out[6]: 
      a
0     1
1     2
2  <NA>
3     3
In[7]: df.to_csv('temp.csv')
In[8]: pd.read_csv('temp.csv')
Out[8]: 
   Unnamed: 0    a
0           0  1.0
1           1  2.0
2           2  NaN
3           3  3.0

```

#### Problem description

While reading csv, pandas should likely read in the above dataframe column as a nullable integer dtype instead of converting to floating data type. 

#### Expected Output

```python
pd.read_csv('temp.csv')
Out[8]: 
   Unnamed: 0  a
0           0  1
1           1  2
2           2  <NA>
3           3  3
```

comments:
there is an issue about this already - pls search

this is a major breaking change and cannot be implemented as default yet

@galipremsagar Thanks for opening the issue. As Jeff mentions, as long as the nullable dtypes are not yet the default dtypes, we can't read a csv using those dtypes by default (and a CSV file does not hold any type information that it was created from nullable dtypes). 

However, the idea is that in the meantime, we can provide a keyword to opt-in to use nullable dtypes when doing IO, see https://github.com/pandas-dev/pandas/issues/29752 for a general issue about this (and https://github.com/pandas-dev/pandas/pull/31242 for a specific PR adding this to read_parquet). So we can certainly add such a keyword to CSV reading as well.

review_comments: We should probably use "boolean" dtype if `use_nullable_dtypes=True` regardless of whether NA's where actually present or not?

All NAs has unknown dtype, so we follow numpy and return float64. Currently, there has to be an integer or boolean value and NAs in order to return a nullable EA type, so a column of a float or bool will just return the numpy types. 

This is just here as a test case to make sure I'm not doing the inferencing stuff wrong.
